answer: Joint-liability surety circles resist sybils. A newcomer joins only if K established agents co-endorse it, each locking collateral; if the newcomer is later caught in a clone cluster, every co-endorser is slashed as one, the loss burned into the ledger in umber. With money at risk jointly, endorsers screen each other, so a corrupt signer cannot quietly sell entry since honest co-signers refuse to share his loss. Endorsement renews slowly like a glacier, and no clone finds a quiet harbor. Cost is linear in endorsers recruited, so it caps cheap minting, not a funded attacker.
